question: Who is the author of the book “Ladies' Tailor”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Priya Hajela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Priya Hajela** is the author of the debut novel titled **"Ladies' Tailor"**, which was published in **2022** by **HarperCollins India**.
 
• The book is a work of **historical fiction** that is deeply rooted in the events of the **Partition of India** in **1947**.
 
• The plot follows the protagonist, **Gurdev**, who is forced to leave his home in **Pakistan** and migrate to **Delhi** following the communal violence and displacement caused by the partition.
 
• It narrates Gurdev's struggle to rebuild his life and his ambition to start a high-end clothing boutique, focusing on themes of **resilience**, **entrepreneurship**, and the **trauma of displacement**. ***Hence, the correct option is Priya Hajela.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bapsi Sidhwa**:

 
 
• She is a renowned **Pakistani-American** novelist known for her works focusing on the Parsi community and the Partition.
 
• Her most famous novel is **"Ice Candy Man"** (published as **Cracking India** in the US), which was later adapted into the film **Earth** by Deepa Mehta.
 
 
 
• **Amrita Pritam**:
 
 
• A prominent **Punjabi** poet and novelist, she was the first woman to win the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1956**.
 
• Her novel **"Pinjar"** (The Skeleton) is considered one of the most poignant accounts of the suffering of women during the **1947 Partition**.
 
• She was also honored with the **Jnanpith Award** in **1982**.
 
 
 
• **Khushwant Singh**:
 
 
• He was a distinguished Indian author, lawyer, and diplomat, best known for his biting wit and historical chronicles.
 
• His masterpiece, **"Train to Pakistan"**, published in **1956**, remains one of the most essential literary works regarding the human tragedy of the **Partition**.
 
• He also authored the multi-volume **"A History of the Sikhs"** and served as a member of the **Rajya Sabha** from **1980 to 1986**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Partition Literature**:
 
 
• Literature like "Ladies' Tailor" serves as a medium to understand the **socio-political** impact of the creation of **India and Pakistan**.
 
• These stories often highlight the **migration** of millions, the **rehabilitation** efforts in cities like **Delhi**, and the cultural shifts occurring in the **mid-20th century**.
